catalog_quote: Tones at the level of syllables are H[igh], L[ow], R[ising] = <LH>, F[alling] = <HL>, and bell-shaped <LHL>. There are no <HLH> syllables. ... In word-nonfinal syllables, contour tones (R, F) must be spread over at least two moras. Word-finally, R-tone must have two moras. Word-finally, F-tone does not require two moras, so there are words ending with F-toned CV syllable (this differentiates Walo from Beni and most other Dogon languages so far studied). ... Except due to grammatically conditioned tone overlays, each stem must have at least one H-tone segment, i.e., at least one H, R, F, or <LHL> syllable. This applies to noun, adjective, numeral, verb, and adverb stems; it does not necessarily apply to functional elements (such as pronominal clitics and clause-final subordinating morphemes). ... new_statements.rule_in_words: Bankan Tey is described purely as a (lexical plus grammatical) tone language: syllables carry H, L, rising, falling or bell-shaped tones, every lexical stem has at least one H-tone element, and verbs are lexically {H} or {LH} with the tone break after the first mora. The grammar makes no statement about word stress or accent; its 'Embryonic metrical structure' section is an unfilled heading.
new_statements.exceptions: Functional elements (pronominal clitics, clause-final subordinators) need not carry an H-tone; Fulfulde loan verbs are {H} regardless of initial consonant. No stress-related exceptions since no stress rule is given.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern lexical stems/words (tone melodies and syllable-level tone); phrase-level effects are treated separately under 3.8 Intonation contours ('dying-quail' final prolongation with HL pitch). The source is a self-described fragmentary draft marked 'not for quotation without permission'; the quoted passage is author's Bankan-Tey-specific text (black type), not grammar-template boilerplate (brown type).
new_statements.identity_note: Heath's grammar describes the Dogon language of Walo (Oualo) village, endonym Bankan Tey (bank1259, ISO dbw); Blench 2005 calls the same variety 'Walo-Kumbe'. Heath initially treated it with Ben Tey (bent1238) as 'Beni-Walo' but separated them; the retired glottocode walo1239 was split into Bankan Tey / Ben Tey. CAVEAT: the only grammar is a self-described 'very fragmentary draft dated November 2014.. not for quotation without permission' (title page), although it is openly hosted by the MPG-run dogonlanguages.info under the site's CC-BY 4.0 notice; the tone passage quoted is in black type (= new Bankan Tey material per the draft's colour code, verified with pdftohtml), not brown template text.

sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent: sec. 2.1 Prosody (p.19) and 3.2.2 'Embryonic metrical structure' (p.20) are empty headings; sec. 3.7 Tones (p.22-23) gives syllable tones H, L, <LH>, <HL>, <LHL>, contour-tone mora requirements, 'each stem must have at least one H-tone segment', verbs lexically {H} or {LH} with tone break near the left edge. Words 'stress'/'accent' never applied to Bankan Tey.
